name: Singapore
summary_text: Singapore is broadly workable — far safer than its neighbour Malaysia, with no criminalisation of trans identity, no religious police, and one of the world's lowest crime rates. Section 377A (which criminalised sex between men) was repealed in 2022, and the prison service reports no assaults against its 10 transgender inmates — unusually positive for axis-H. Singapore is also a regional medical hub with gender-affirming care available. The main gaps: legal gender recognition requires genital surgery (expensive and restrictive), there is no anti-discrimination law (the 2025 Workplace Fairness Act explicitly excludes sexual orientation and gender identity), and over 65% of trans Singaporeans report negative workplace experiences. A radio code still groups homosexuality with "paedophilia and incest" as lifestyles barred from the airwaves. Progress has "stalled" since the 377A repeal, with discrimination "quietly tolerated." For a visitor: efficient border processing, very low street crime, unrestricted bathrooms, and no trans-specific police friction. The atmosphere is conservative but quietly accommodating in practice.

sources.claim_summary: TransgenderSG/Transbefrienders/NUS study 'Measuring Public Sentiments and Challenges Faced by Singapore's Transgender and Gender-Diverse Community' (Feb 2025): comprehensive survey covering demographics, school experiences, employment barriers and discrimination, healthcare access, gender-affirming care costs and experiences, and cisgender perspectives.

sources.title: Singapore | Outright International
sources.claim_summary: Outright International country overview (updated March 2026): Section 377A repealed in 2022 (effective January 2023), but the constitution was simultaneously amended to codify marriage as between a man and a woman; adoption restrictions; trans people can change gender markers conditional on gender-affirming surgery; trans youth can access HRT with both parents' consent (16+ private, 18+ public), with much stricter access under 21.

sources.title: 10 transgender persons behind bars, no assaults against such inmates reported: S’pore prisons | The Straits Times
sources.claim_summary: Straits Times (Nov 2023): 10 transgender inmates behind bars in Singapore (one post-surgery, nine transitioning), with no assaults reported, per the Singapore Prison Service - raised in Parliament after the Scottish Isla Bryson case; housing arrangements discussed.

sources.title: Workplace Fairness? Not for LGBTQ+ Workers | Pink Dot SG
sources.claim_summary: Pink Dot SG (Jan 2025): the new Workplace Fairness Legislation conspicuously and explicitly excludes sexual orientation and gender identity - 'leaves the LGBTQ+ community empty-handed yet again'; a 2024 Pink Dot study found 69% of LGBTQ+ people encountered discrimination or harassment in hiring or at work; trans workers face some of the most severe discrimination including hiring barriers and safety threats.
NOTE: Not retrievable at research time (HTTP 401); the underlying Reuters feature (June 2023) covers Singapore's LGBT community feeling safer as the end of the 377A ban brings change.

sources.title: Singapore radio code’s grouping of homosexuality with criminal acts sparks calls for review | South China Morning Post
sources.claim_summary: SCMP (July 2025): Singapore's radio broadcast code groups homosexuality with paedophilia and incest as 'lifestyles' not allowed on air - a former DJ and a blogger call for review, saying the clause 'has no place in post-377A Singapore'.

sources.title: Singapore - F&M Global Barometers
sources.claim_summary: F&M Global Barometers country profile for Singapore: composite LGBT-rights perception scores including the Global Barometer of Transgender Rights index.

sources.title: LGBTQIA+ travel in Singapore | Intrepid Travel US
sources.claim_summary: Intrepid Travel country guide: LGBTQIA+ travellers to Singapore 'are welcomed and supported' though discretion with public displays of affection is recommended; notes Pink Dot rallies since 2009 and a gay-friendly bar scene.

sources.title: singapore government awards S$100,000 grant to group with ex-gay affiliation | Gay News Asia
sources.claim_summary: Fridae (Jan 2006) by Sylvia Tan: the Singapore government awarded a S$100,000 grant to Liberty League, a group claiming to help gays and lesbians 'understand' their sexual identity - Fridae uncovered its links to an international Christian ex-gay/reparative-therapy network; founder Leslie Lung is a self-described ex-transsexual.
